title: Event-Driven Agent Triggers
summary: Start bounded agent work from meaningful business events using durable publication, deduplicated consumption, and explicit event-to-task ownership.
overview: Event-driven triggers initiate agent work when a business fact changes, such as a shipment delay, new document, or equipment alarm. Events should describe an occurrence with identity, source, type, time, and relevant business keys. They should not be treated as commands that automatically authorize every action an agent might infer.

Separate event transport from decision logic. A consumer verifies relevance, policy, freshness, and deduplication before creating a task. Because delivery and ordering guarantees vary, design for duplicates and late arrivals. CloudEvents provides a standard event envelope, but application semantics, authorization, and recovery remain the system's responsibility.

production.poc: A prototype can subscribe to one event type and record which events would create useful tasks. Shadow operation reveals noisy triggers before automation is enabled.
production.production: Production uses reliable publication, schema validation, deduplication, and bounded consumer concurrency. Store the causal link between the original event and every generated task.
production.scale: At scale, partition events by meaningful entity keys, apply coalescing or debounce policies for noisy sources, and monitor lag. Agent-generated events need origin markers or loop detection to prevent self-triggering storms.

components.name: Event producer
components.role: Emits committed business facts through an outbox or equivalent reliable publication boundary.

components.name: Event bus
components.role: Routes and buffers events while preserving documented delivery and partition semantics.

components.name: Trigger evaluator
components.role: Checks schema, freshness, relevance, policy, and duplicate identity.

components.name: Task launcher
components.role: Creates a durable bounded operation linked to the event and business entity.

components.name: Loop and rate controller
components.role: Suppresses recursive triggers and limits bursts from noisy event sources.

flow.title: Publish occurrence
flow.description: Record the business change and event identity consistently with the system of record.

flow.title: Validate envelope
flow.description: Check source identity, event type, schema version, timestamps, and required entity keys.

flow.title: Deduplicate and order
flow.description: Reject repeats and apply entity-version rules to stale or out-of-order events.

flow.title: Evaluate trigger
flow.description: Decide whether the change warrants agent work or can be coalesced with an existing task.

flow.title: Launch bounded task
flow.description: Persist causal metadata, permissions context, deadline, and operation identity before dispatch.

flow.title: Acknowledge and observe
flow.description: Acknowledge accepted handling and monitor task outcomes, event lag, and recursion indicators.

useCase.title: Responding to refrigerated shipment delays
useCase.situation: A cold-chain distributor receives location and temperature events from carriers throughout a shipment's journey.
useCase.problem: Triggering an agent on every update creates repeated investigations and conflicting customer messages during a single delay.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must investigate material delay changes and prepare one current response per affected shipment.
useCase.architecture: A trigger service validates events, groups them by shipment, and launches a bounded assessment only when policy thresholds or status versions change.
runtime: A delayed-arrival event updates the shipment state; related telemetry is coalesced into the same investigation window.
The agent checks product handling constraints and delivery alternatives, then prepares a notification linked to the originating event set.
useCase.failure: If an older on-time event arrives later, entity-version checks prevent it from cancelling the active delay investigation.
useCase.impact: Track trigger-to-start latency, duplicate suppression, event lag, and investigations per business incident rather than raw event consumption throughput alone.

tradeoffs.benefit: Work begins close to the relevant business change.
tradeoffs.cost: Noisy sources can create expensive bursts.

tradeoffs.benefit: Producers and agent workers can evolve independently.
tradeoffs.cost: Schema compatibility and eventual consistency need active management.

tradeoffs.benefit: Repeated changes become one coherent investigation.
tradeoffs.cost: Waiting windows may delay response to important updates.

failures.scenario: Agent output produces the same trigger again
failures.detection: Causality metadata reveals repeated origin and entity cycles.
failures.recovery: Suppress recursive launches and alert on the loop.

failures.scenario: An event is published without its business commit
failures.detection: Consumer cannot find the referenced authoritative state.
failures.recovery: Use reliable publication and retry only within a bounded freshness window.

mistakes.fix: Resolve current identity and policy before actions.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming delivery is unique and ordered
mistakes.fix: Deduplicate and validate entity versions explicitly.

mistakes.mistake: Launching one agent per telemetry sample
mistakes.fix: Aggregate meaningful incidents before expensive processing.

whenToUse: Business changes require timely bounded investigation.
Producers and workers need independent scaling.
Event identity and entity state can support deduplication.
whenNotToUse: A synchronous user response is the actual requirement.
Source events are too unreliable to establish business facts.
Polling a small stable dataset is simpler and sufficient.
checklist: Version event schemas and validate envelopes.
Publish events consistently with business commits.
Monitor lag and incident-level trigger volume.
